items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: under the auspices of Jon Faddis, a great trumpet player and friend

ctx.x: That’s a good analogy. Can you remember the conversation that you had with him that led to the educational—

Oh well it was — I met Louis about — well you see I used to work for Louis part time. In other words Mr. Glaser was Louis Armstrong’s manager and he would call me and I was working let’s say at Rockefeller Center at that time, and he’d call and he’d say, “Phoebe, © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

Pops wants you to come out and do this and this and this.” So I’d take the day off and I’d do whatever Louis wanted because I just had a thing about Louis and he knew that he could count on me for anything. So he called me that day and I called him back I says, “Mr. Glaser says you need me.” He said, “Well I want you to get the lawyer and I’d like him to” — Ellis his name was — “I’d like him to meet us for lunch, I’ve got to talk to you.” I met him for lunch and he gives me a check for $40,000. In 1969 now, that…
